verdict.rationale: Honeybadger lets users define Alarms, which pair a BadgerQL query with a threshold and fire alerts when it is exceeded. It also has built-in event-driven automations: auto-resolving errors on deploy, notifying the team on deploy, and anomaly-detection alerts that route to integrations such as PagerDuty and Slack. However, the user-defined triggers mostly produce notifications rather than arbitrary actions, and no general rules or workflow engine is documented. Missing for 10: a general-purpose rule engine with configurable conditions and actions (e.g. auto-assign, auto-tag, run a webhook or workflow on match), documentation of how to customize the built-in automations, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
